label_assessment.finding: Publisher supplies benign capture provenance and attack schedules but no timezone-qualified per-query labels among the local files. Mixed attack captures include background queries. Do not infer labels from folder/file names.
label_assessment.benign_fallback: Use only the two publisher-designated benign recordings, with one capture for training and one for preliminary validation. This is an operational benign-reference assumption, not independent per-query ground truth.
label_assessment.attack_schedule_caution: Published local clock schedules cannot be silently mapped to UTC; the first light-image query in this local capture is at 2020-11-22 01:46 UTC, and published session boundaries need explicit validation.
label_assessment.candidate_caution: Matching the publisher attack-domain description is supporting evidence, not automatic per-query ground truth; one recovered candidate does not establish representative 20-query attack sequences.

training_recommendation: Prepare benign-only sequence autoencoder. Exclude response-derived and capture-artifact features by default. Do not train a supervised classifier on the current provenance categories.
extractor_ordering_limitation: The existing extractor associates responses in packet-file order, then sorts extracted queries. Capture timestamp regressions can therefore cause missed matches. This audit does not silently repair those associations.
limitations: Recognized nonstandard-port DNS is counted by TShark; concealed/encrypted DNS and arbitrary protocols are not exhaustively ruled out.
